en: The Sūtra of the Great Brightness Heart Dhāraṇī of the Invincible One,
translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, the Court-Dispersing Grandee, Acting Assistant Director of the Court of State Ceremonial,
and Great Master of the Propagation of the Teaching, the Subject Fǎtián, by Imperial Decree.
I take refuge in the Unsurpassed Awakening, as well as the Dharma and the Assembly of Noble Sages.
This Great Illuminating Heart Mantra was spoken by the Invincible One himself;
the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, has also spoken this vidyā.
It benefits all sentient beings,
accomplishes all auspicious undertakings,
eliminates grave offenses, and prevents untimely death.
Their lifespan will be extended and they will be free from all illnesses.
If there are good men or good women, or boys or girls,
who revere and honor this sutra, [they shall likewise attain these benefits].
All humans and non-humans who harbor malicious intent,
including rākṣasas, uśtarakas, pretas, skandhas, apasmāras, yakṣas, mātṛs, bhūtas, and malevolent spirits.
The various evil assemblies have practiced perverted dharmas,
casting curses upon sentient beings so that they are born into diverse realms and suffer from hunger, disease, and all manner of malignant illnesses.
Such sufferings as sores, carbuncles, abscesses, swellings, scabies, leprosy,
and warts shall be unable to harm them;
even if they possess the karmic retribution of past transgressions.
When they are oppressed and distressed by such calamities as mutual killing,
harm, strife, litigation, and disputes, as well as royal legal prohibitions,
imprisonment, water, fire, and the perils of thieves; at such times—
By recollecting, reading, and reciting [this], calamities will certainly dissipate,
and one will be free from misfortune, attaining auspiciousness and peace.
Furthermore, if there is another person...
One may write this vidyā upon birch bark, silk, or paper;
or write it in another location and make offerings to it;
or wear it upon the crown of the head or around the neck.
Whether worn on the upper arm or the hand, or carried within one's garments,
or fashioned into a garland and placed upon the topknot of the head—
by thus receiving and maintaining it, one shall forever be free from calamities and constantly attain peace and happiness.
If one constantly recites this at dawn with a pure body and mind and sincere devotion,
after one's life has ended, one will attain the knowledge of past lives throughout seven successive births;
one’s physical appearance will be upright and majestic, and one will always experience happiness.
Perfectly endowed with the practice of ethical discipline,
his mouth constantly emits the fragrance of the *utpala* lotus;
his speech is truthful and sincere, and he is cherished and respected by all people.
Furthermore, one shall be reborn in the Heaven of the Thirty-three.
By visualizing according to the ritual rules of this mantra, one will certainly attain accomplishment.
Then he spoke the dhāraṇī, saying:
Tadyathā: jambhani, stambhani, mohani, dhadadhada, dhaṃsiya, ya ya ya ya, ṭiha ṭiha ṭiha ṭiha, ṭi parakaraṇi, amoghe.
Rye virya kumbhavāri yunatīti bhūtakarṇanāda karikumbhavāti viśa kumbhavāti sarvamale bhūtamale ḍaḥ.
kṣa kṣaṃ śrī-dharma-karase-nasva sarvabhūta-rāṃ sarva-viśva-vidhe sarva-vyādhi-vidhe.
Svāhā sarvabuddhānām abhiṣekam dadāmi svāhā | tadyathā | siddhakari siddharite siddhamanorathe siddhakārye hūru jūru miśra ||
vaḥsati prasavasati satti satti siddharite nirghātarīye vātīgamani tapani śaraṇi.
